commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: plugin-authoring
commands.description: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.

commands.name: implement
commands.description: Execute sprint tasks with production-quality code and tests (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: review-sprint
commands.description: Validate sprint implementation against acceptance criteria (from pr/head/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under pr/head/) (project)

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.name: color
commands.description: Set the prompt bar color for this session

commands.name: context

commands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Manage MCP servers

commands.name: model
commands.description: Set the AI model for Claude Code

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

' <<<"$MAP_JSON" >> "$ERRORS"

while IFS= read -r spath; do
    [[ -n "$spath" ]] || continue
    case "$spath" in /*|*..*) echo "gate or policy script '$spath' must be a repository-relative path" >> "$ERRORS"; continue ;; esac
    [[ -f "$ROOT/$spath" ]] || echo "gate or policy script $spath does not exist" >> "$ERRORS"

if [[ -s "$ERRORS" ]]; then
    sed "s/^/$SCRIPT_NAME: /" "$ERRORS" >&2

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- renderers
# Shared cell sanitiser: control characters removed, pipes escaped for GFM tables.
JQ_DEFS='
  def cell: tostring | explode | map(select(. >= 32 and . != 127)) | implode | gsub("\\|"; "\\|");
  def kinds: ["hook", "fence", "validator", "gate", "policy"];
  def regs: if (.registrations // []) | length == 0 then "-" else (.registrations | map("`" + cell + "`") | join(", ")) end;
  def origin_txt: .origin as $o | if ($o.ref | tostring | startswith($o.kind | tostring)) then ($o.ref | tostring) else "\($o.kind) \($o.ref)" end;
  def yesno: if . == true then "yes" else "no" end;
'

render_register() {
    jq -r "$JQ_DEFS"'
      .guards as $g
      | "# Guard register",
        "",
        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh from .claude/settings.json, the fence and validator markers and .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml. Do not edit by hand: edit the origin map and regenerate (.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table); CI runs --check. -->",
        "",
        "Every guard Loa ships, with its class, status, origin, knob and floor flag. Structural only: the 30-day yield of a host is untracked, in `.run/guard-yield.md` and `.run/guard-yield.json` (regenerate with `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`). Classes: harness (the model cannot override it), script (a script checks or reports), prose (the model is asked to comply). Status: dormant means armed only by the env var in the knob column; telemetry means it observes and never refuses.",
        "",
        "- guards: \($g | length)",
        "- guards_without_origin: \($g | map(select((.origin.ref // "") == "")) | length)",
        "- dormant: \($g | map(select(.status == "dormant")) | length)",
        "- floor: \($g | map(select(.floor == true)) | length)",
        (kinds[] as $k | ($g | map(select(.kind == $k))) as $rows | select($rows | length > 0)
          | "",
            "## \($k) (\($rows | length))",
            "",
            "| id | class | status | origin | knob | floor | registrations |",
            "|----|-------|--------|--------|------|-------|---------------|",
            ($rows[] | "| \(.id | cell) | \(.class | cell) | \(.status | cell) | \(origin_txt | cell) | \(.knob | cell) | \(.floor | yesno) | \(regs) |"))
    ' <<<"$MAP_JSON"
}

render_hooks_block() {
    jq -r --argjson hooks "$HOOKS_JSON" "$JQ_DEFS"'
      (.guards | map({key: .id, value: .}) | from_entries) as $by
      | "<!-- guard-register:begin -->",
        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table from .claude/settings.json and .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml; do not edit by hand. Full register: grimoires/loa/guards.md -->",
        "| Event | Matcher | Script | Status | Knob | Purpose |",
        "|-------|---------|--------|--------|------|---------|",
        ($hooks[] | . as $h | $by[$h.id] as $r
          | "| \($h.event | cell) | \(if $h.matcher == "" then "(all)" else ($h.matcher | cell) end) | `\(if $h.wrapped then "hook-guard.sh " else "" end)\($h.id | ltrimstr("hook:") | cell)` | \($r.status | cell) | \($r.knob | cell) | \($r.note // "" | cell) |"),
        "<!-- guard-register:end -->"
    ' <<<"$MAP_JSON"
}

# Rewrites the marker block of $HOOKS_REF into $2 (exit 3 when the markers are absent or repeated).
render_hooks_ref() {
    local block="$1" dest="$2" nb ne
    [[ -f "$HOOKS_REF" && -r "$HOOKS_REF" ]] || die 3 "hooks reference not readable: $HOOKS_REF"
    nb="$(grep -c '^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$' "$HOOKS_REF" || true)"
    ne="$(grep -c '^<!-- guard-register:end -->$' "$HOOKS_REF" || true)"
    [[ "$nb" == "1" && "$ne" == "1" ]] \
        || die 3 "$HOOKS_REF needs exactly one <!-- guard-register:begin --> and one <!-- guard-register:end --> line (found $nb and $ne)"
    awk -v blockfile="$block" '
      /^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$/ { while ((getline l < blockfile) > 0) print l; skip = 1; next }
      /^<!-- guard-register:end -->$/ { skip = 0; next }
      !skip { print }
    ' "$HOOKS_REF" > "$dest"
}

# Atomic replace: temp beside the destination, then rename.
install_file() {
    local src="$1" dest="$2" tmp
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
    tmp="$(mktemp "$(dirname "$dest")/.$(basename "$dest").XXXXXX")"
    cat "$src" > "$tmp"
    chmod 0644 "$tmp"
    mv -f "$tmp" "$dest"
}

REGISTER_NEW="$TMPWORK/guards.md"
render_register > "$REGISTER_NEW"
HOOKS_BLOCK="$TMPWORK/hooks-block.md"
render_hooks_block > "$HOOKS_BLOCK"
HOOKS_REF_NEW="$TMPWORK/hooks-reference.md"
N_GUARDS="$(jq '.guards | length' <<<"$MAP_JSON")"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- --check
if (( DO_CHECK )); then
    render_hooks_ref "$HOOKS_BLOCK" "$HOOKS_REF_NEW"
    drift=0
    if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]] || ! cmp -s "$REGISTER_NEW" "$OUT"; then
        echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: drift: $OUT differs from the generated register" >&2
        diff -u "$OUT" "$REGISTER_NEW" 2>/dev/null | head -20 >&2 || true
        drift=1
    fi
    if ! cmp -s "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" "$HOOKS_REF"; then
        echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: drift: the guard-register table in $HOOKS_REF differs from the generated one" >&2
        diff -u "$HOOKS_REF" "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" 2>/dev/null | head -20 >&2 || true
        drift=1
    fi
    if (( drift )); then
        echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: $REGEN_HINT" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: in sync ($N_GUARDS guards)"
    exit 0
fi

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- yield
SEGMENTS="$TMPWORK/segments"
: > "$SEGMENTS"
for f in "$AUDIT_LOG" "$AUDIT_LOG".*; do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
    [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || die 3 "audit log segment not readable: $f"
    printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$SEGMENTS"
done
N_SEGMENTS="$(wc -l < "$SEGMENTS" | tr -d ' ')"
ROWS="$TMPWORK/audit.rows"
: > "$ROWS"
if [[ "$N_SEGMENTS" == "0" ]]; then
    warn "no audit log at $AUDIT_LOG (or segments $AUDIT_LOG.*); the yield is empty"
else
    while IFS= read -r f; do cat -- "$f" >> "$ROWS"; printf '\n' >> "$ROWS"; done < "$SEGMENTS"
fi

TMP_PREFIX="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
TMP_PREFIX="${TMP_PREFIX%/}/"
MAIN_ROOT=""
if common="$(cd "$ROOT" && git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)"; then
    common="$(cd "$ROOT" && cd "$common" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || common=""
    case "$common" in */.git) MAIN_ROOT="${common%/.git}" ;; esac
fi

# Heredoc classification: the FR-6 classifier when present (heredoc_nonexec <command>
# returns 0 for a heredoc whose consumer does not execute it), else `<<` presence.
NONEXEC_IDX='null'
if [[ -f "$HEREDOC_LIB" ]] && grep -q '^heredoc_nonexec[[:space:]]*()' "$HEREDOC_LIB"; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    if source "$HEREDOC_LIB" 2>/dev/null && declare -F heredoc_nonexec >/dev/null; then
        IDX_FILE="$TMPWORK/nonexec.idx"
        : > "$IDX_FILE"
        # Same row indexing as the join below: non-blank lines, in order. Commands travel base64-encoded.
        while IFS="$US" read -r idx b64; do
            [[ -n "$idx" ]] || continue
            cmd="$(printf '%s' "$b64" | base64 --decode 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$b64" | base64 -D 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if heredoc_nonexec "$cmd" 2>/dev/null; then printf '%s\n' "$idx" >> "$IDX_FILE"; fi
        done < <(jq -R -n -r '[inputs | select(test("\\S")) | (try fromjson catch null)] | to_entries[]
                   | select((.value | type) == "object" and .value.action == "block" and ((.value.command // "") | tostring | contains("<<")))
                   | "\(.key)\u001f\(.value.command | tostring | @base64)"' "$ROWS" 2>/dev/null)
        NONEXEC_IDX="$(jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | tonumber)' "$IDX_FILE")"
    fi
fi

YIELD_JSON="$(jq -R -n \
    --argjson map "$MAP_JSON" \
    --argjson hooks "$HOOKS_JSON" \
    --argjson nonexec "$NONEXEC_IDX" \
    --argjson now "$NOW_EPOCH" \
    --argjson win "$WINDOW_DAYS" \
    --argjson segs "$N_SEGMENTS" \
    --argjson burst_rows "$BURST_ROWS" \
    --arg tmp "$TMP_PREFIX" \
    --arg root "$ROOT" \
    --arg mainroot "$MAIN_ROOT" '
  def epoch: (.ts // .timestamp // null) | if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
  def under($r): . as $c | ($r != "") and ($c == $r or ($c | startswith($r + "/")));
  def minute: (.ts // .timestamp // "") | tostring | .[0:16];
  def replay($burst): (.replay == true)
    or ((.cwd // "") | type == "string" and (startswith($tmp) or contains("/bats-run-") or contains("/bats.") or contains("/evals/results/") or contains("/sandbox/")))
    or (minute | IN($burst[]));
  def outside_repo: (.cwd // "") as $c | ($c | type == "string") and $c != "" and (($c | under($root)) or ($c | under($mainroot)) | not);
  def verbs: ["rm","git","find","dd","mkfs","shred","truncate","kubectl","terraform","aws","gcloud","psql","mysql","DROP","DELETE","TRUNCATE"];
  def destructive_start: (.command // "") | tostring | [splits("(;|&&|\\|\\||\\||\n)")] | map(sub("^\\s+"; "") | (split("\\s+"; null)[0] // "")) | any(.[]; IN(verbs[]));
  def heredoc: if $nonexec == null then ((.command // "") | tostring | contains("<<")) else (._i | IN($nonexec[])) end;
  def prose_class: (.pattern_id // "") | IN("SP-1", "FR-MERGE-2", "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS");
  def likely_fp: heredoc or outside_repo or (prose_class and (destructive_start | not));
  def day: strftime("%Y-%m-%d");
  def origin_txt: .origin as $o | if ($o.ref | tostring | startswith($o.kind | tostring)) then ($o.ref | tostring) else "\($o.kind) \($o.ref)" end;
  ($hooks | map({key: (.rel | split("/") | last | sub("\\.sh$"; "")), value: .id}) | from_entries) as $hookid
  | ($map.guards | map(.id)) as $known
  | [inputs | select(test("\\S")) | (try fromjson catch null)] as $raw
  | ($raw | to_entries | map(.value as $v | if ($v | type) == "object" then ($v + {_i: .key}) else null end)) as $all
  | ($all | map(select(. != null))) as $rows
  | ($rows | length) as $read
  | ($rows | map(select(.action == "block" or .hook == "implement-gate") | . + {_t: epoch})) as $cand
  | ($cand | map(select(._t != null and ._t >= ($now - $win * 86400) and ._t <= ($now + 86400)))) as $inwin
  | ($inwin | map(select(.action == "block" and .replay != true)) | group_by(minute)
     | map(select(length >= $burst_rows) | .[0] | minute)) as $burst
  | ($inwin | map(select(replay($burst) | not))) as $live
  | ($live | map(
      (if .hook == "block-destructive-bash" then
         ["hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"] + (if ((.pattern_id // "") | tostring | test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$")) then ["fence:" + .pattern_id] else [] end)
       elif .hook == "implement-gate" then ["hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh", "gate:implement-gate"]
       elif ((.hook // "") | type) == "string" and $hookid[.hook] != null then [$hookid[.hook]]
       else [] end) as $ids
      | {ids: ($ids | map(select(IN($known[])))),
         block: (.action == "block" or .action == "deny"),
         telemetry: (.action == "telemetry" or .action == "ask"),
         fp: ((.action == "block" or .action == "deny") and likely_fp),
         t: ._t})) as $cls
  | ($cls | map(.ids[]) | unique) as $seen
  | (["hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh", "hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh", "gate:implement-gate"]
     + ($map.guards | map(select(.kind == "fence") | .id)) + $seen | unique) as $writers
  | ($map.guards | map(. as $g
      | if ($g.id | IN($writers[])) then
          ($cls | map(select(any(.ids[]; . == $g.id)))) as $mine
          | ($mine | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | map(.t) | max) as $last
          | {id, kind, class, status, origin: origin_txt, knob, floor, registrations: (.registrations // []), audited: true,
             blocks_30d: ($mine | map(select(.block)) | length),
             likely_fp_30d: ($mine | map(select(.fp)) | length),
             telemetry_30d: ($mine | map(select(.telemetry)) | length),
             last_real_catch: (if $last == null then "none in window" else ($last | day) end)}
        else
          {id, kind, class, status, origin: origin_txt, knob, floor, registrations: (.registrations // []), audited: false,
           blocks_30d: null, likely_fp_30d: null, telemetry_30d: null, last_real_catch: "n/a"}
        end)) as $guards
  | {
      schema_version: 1,
      generated_at: ($now | day),
      window_days: $win,
      scope: "host",
      audit_segments: $segs,
      audit_rows_read: $read,
      audit_rows_unparseable: (($raw | length) - $read),
      audit_rows_considered: ($inwin | length),
      replay_rows_excluded: (($inwin | length) - ($live | length)),
      replay_rows_by_rule: {
        flag: ($inwin | map(select(.replay == true)) | length),
        cwd: ($inwin | map(select(.replay != true and replay([]))) | length),
        burst: ($inwin | map(select(.replay != true and (replay([]) | not) and replay($burst))) | length)
      },
      heuristic: "likely_fp = heredoc in the command OR cwd outside the repository OR (pattern SP-1, FR-MERGE-2 or FR-2-AMBIGUOUS with no destructive verb at statement start); real = block AND NOT likely_fp",
      totals: {
        guards: ($map.guards | length),
        guards_without_origin: 0,
        dormant: ($map.guards | map(select(.status == "dormant")) | length),
        blocks_30d: ($cls | map(select(.block)) | length),
        real_blocks_30d: ($cls | map(select(.block and (.fp | not))) | length),
        likely_fp_30d: ($cls | map(select(.fp)) | length),
        telemetry_30d: ($cls | map(select(.telemetry)) | length),
        unattributed_30d: ($cls | map(select(.ids | length == 0)) | length)
      },
      guards: $guards
    }
' "$ROWS")" || die 3 "the audit log could not be joined"

render_yield_md() {
    jq -r "$JQ_DEFS"'
      def n: if . == null then "n/a" else tostring end;
      . as $y
      | "# Guard yield (host)",
        "",
        "<!-- Generated by .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh; untracked, host-local. The structural register is grimoires/loa/guards.md. -->",
        "",
        "- generated_at: \($y.generated_at)",
        "- window_days: \($y.window_days)",
        "- scope: \($y.scope)",
        "- audit_segments: \($y.audit_segments)",
        "- audit_rows_considered: \($y.audit_rows_considered)",
        "- replay_rows_excluded: \($y.replay_rows_excluded) (flag \($y.replay_rows_by_rule.flag), cwd \($y.replay_rows_by_rule.cwd), burst \($y.replay_rows_by_rule.burst))",
        "- audit_rows_unparseable: \($y.audit_rows_unparseable)",
        "- totals: \($y.totals.real_blocks_30d) real blocks, \($y.totals.likely_fp_30d) likely FP, \($y.totals.telemetry_30d) telemetry, \($y.totals.unattributed_30d) unattributed",
        "- heuristic: \($y.heuristic | cell)",
        (kinds[] as $k | ($y.guards | map(select(.kind == $k))) as $rows | select($rows | length > 0)
          | "",
            "## \($k) (\($rows | length))",
            "",
            "| id | class | status | origin | knob | floor | registrations | blocks_30d | likely_fp_30d | telemetry_30d | last_real_catch |",
            "|----|-------|--------|--------|------|-------|---------------|------------|---------------|---------------|-----------------|",
            ($rows[] | "| \(.id | cell) | \(.class | cell) | \(.status | cell) | \(.origin | cell) | \(.knob | cell) | \(.floor | yesno) | \(regs) | \(.blocks_30d | n) | \(.likely_fp_30d | n) | \(.telemetry_30d | n) | \(.last_real_catch | cell) |"))
    ' <<<"$YIELD_JSON"
}

YIELD_MD_NEW="$TMPWORK/guard-yield.md"
YIELD_JSON_NEW="$TMPWORK/guard-yield.json"
render_yield_md > "$YIELD_MD_NEW"
jq '.' <<<"$YIELD_JSON" > "$YIELD_JSON_NEW"

install_file "$REGISTER_NEW" "$OUT"
install_file "$YIELD_MD_NEW" "$YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.md"
install_file "$YIELD_JSON_NEW" "$YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.json"
if (( DO_HOOKS_TABLE )); then
    render_hooks_ref "$HOOKS_BLOCK" "$HOOKS_REF_NEW"
    cmp -s "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" "$HOOKS_REF" || install_file "$HOOKS_REF_NEW" "$HOOKS_REF"
fi

summary="$(jq -r '"\(.totals.guards) guards (\(.totals.dormant) dormant); \(.window_days) d: \(.totals.real_blocks_30d) real blocks, \(.totals.likely_fp_30d) likely FP, \(.replay_rows_excluded) replay rows excluded; scope host"' <<<"$YIELD_JSON")"
if (( DO_JSON )); then
    cat "$YIELD_JSON_NEW"
    echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: wrote $OUT and $YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.{md,json}: $summary" >&2
else
    echo "$SCRIPT_NAME: wrote $OUT and $YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.{md,json}: $summary"
fi
exit 0

208:_drop_paragraph() {

210:import re, sys
211:path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

257:        fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}

   283	# The suite-level STATUS.json merges every batch: counters add per arm; the
   284	# state is failed > running > partial > complete; source/model must agree.
   285	aggregate_status() {
   286	  local agg="$SUITE_DIR/STATUS.json" lockd="$SUITE_DIR/.status.lock" n=0
   287	  until mkdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null; do n=$((n + 1)); [[ $n -gt 50 ]] && return 0; sleep 0.1; done
   288	  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
   289	  jq -s --arg suite "$SUITE" '
   290	    def rank: {"failed": 4, "running": 3, "partial": 2, "complete": 1}[.] // 4;
   291	    (map(.state) | max_by(rank)) as $state |
   292	    {schema_version: 1, suite: $suite, state: $state,
   293	     batches: map({batch, state, started, finished}),
   294	     per_arm: (reduce (.[] | .per_arm | to_entries[]) as $e ({};
   295	        .[$e.key] |= {trials_done: ((.trials_done // 0) + $e.value.trials_done),
   296	                      trials_failed: ((.trials_failed // 0) + $e.value.trials_failed),
   297	                      trials_planned: ((.trials_planned // 0) + $e.value.trials_planned)})),
   298	     source_commit: (map(.source_commit) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   299	     model_id: (map(.model_id) | unique | if length == 1 then .[0] else "MIXED" end),
   300	     started: (map(.started) | min), finished: (if $state == "running" then null else (map(.finished) | max) end)}' \
   301	    $(find "$SUITE_DIR" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -name STATUS.json | sort) > "$agg.tmp" 2>/dev/null \
   302	    && mv "$agg.tmp" "$agg"
   303	  rmdir "$lockd" 2>/dev/null || true
   304	}

   307	# --- one trial (runs in a background job; writes its row to $JOBS_DIR/<id>.row)
   308	is_transport_failure() {  # is_transport_failure <sandbox-ws>
   309	  local ws="$1" out="$1/.eval/agent-output.json" err="$1/.eval/agent-stderr.log" rc
   310	  rc="$(jq -r '.exit_code // 0' "$ws/.eval/executor.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   311	  case "$rc" in 124|137|143) return 0 ;; esac
   312	  [[ "$(jq -r '.subtype // ""' "$out" 2>/dev/null)" == "missing" ]] && return 0
   313	  [[ -n "$(jq -r '.api_error_status // empty' "$out" 2>/dev/null)" ]] && return 0
   314	  grep -qiE 'rate.?limit|overloaded|session limit|usage limit|out of extra usage|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|network|socket hang up|5[0-9][0-9] ' \
   315	    "$err" "$out" 2>/dev/null && return 0
   316	  return 1

   319	run_trial() {  # run_trial <job-id> <arm> <fixture> <trial>
   320	  local jid="$1" arm="$2" fx="$3" trial="$4"
   321	  local task="$EVALS_DIR/tasks/$SUITE/$TASK_PREFIX-$fx.yaml" task_id="$TASK_PREFIX-$fx"
   322	  local run_id="arms-$SUITE-$BATCH" attempt=0 ws="" trial_id status="error" err_json='null'
   323	  local graders='[]' composite='{"strategy":"all_must_pass","pass":false,"score":0}' executor='null'
   324	  local start_ms end_ms per_trial ex_rc
   325	  per_trial="$(yq -r '.timeout.per_trial // 1500' "$task")"
   326	  start_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   327	  if ! verify_corpus "$fx" >"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.digest" 2>"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift"; then
   328	    printf 'DRIFT\n' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag"; return 0
   329	  fi
   330	  while [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; do
   331	    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
   332	    trial_id="$run_id-$arm-$fx-t$trial-a$attempt-$jid"
   333	    ws="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/sandbox.sh" create --fixture "review-prs/$fx" --run-id "$run_id" --trial-id "$trial_id" 2>/dev/null)" \
   334	      || { err_json='{"type":"infrastructure_error","message":"sandbox creation failed"}'; break; }
   335	    ex_rc=0
   336	    EVAL_PROMPT_TREE="$WORKTREE" EVAL_MODEL="$MODEL" LOA_EVAL_ARM="$arm" LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE="$SUITE_FILE" \
   337	      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT="$SRC_FULL" LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 \
   338	      "$SCRIPT_DIR/execute-agent.sh" --task-yaml "$task" --workspace "$ws" \
   339	        --run-id "$run_id" --trial-id "$trial_id" --timeout "$per_trial" \
   340	        >/dev/null 2>"$JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log" || ex_rc=$?
   341	    [[ -f "$ws/.eval/executor.json" ]] && executor="$(cat "$ws/.eval/executor.json")"
   342	    if [[ $ex_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
   343	      local gout gexit=0
   344	      gout="$("$SCRIPT_DIR/grade.sh" --task-yaml "$task" --workspace "$ws" \
   345	        --timeout "$(yq -r '.timeout.per_grader // 60' "$task")" 2>/dev/null)" || gexit=$?
   346	      if jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$gout"; then
   347	        graders="$(jq -c '.graders' <<<"$gout")"; composite="$(jq -c '.composite' <<<"$gout")"
   348	      fi
   349	      if [[ $gexit -le 1 ]]; then status="completed"; err_json='null'
   350	      else err_json='{"type":"infrastructure_error","message":"grader error"}'; fi
   351	      break
   352	    fi
   353	    if [[ $ex_rc -eq 1 ]] && is_transport_failure "$ws"; then
   354	      err_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$attempt" '{type:"transport_error",message:"executor transport failure",attempt:$a}')"
   355	      if [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; then
   356	        keep_artifacts "$ws" "$arm" "$task_id" "$trial" "-attempt1"
   357	        "$SCRIPT_DIR/sandbox.sh" destroy --trial-id "$trial_id" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   358	        ws=""; executor='null'
   359	        sleep "$RETRY_WAIT"; continue
   360	      fi
   361	    else
   362	      err_json="$(jq -cn --argjson rc "$ex_rc" '{type:(if $rc == 2 then "infrastructure_error" else "agent_error" end),message:("execute-agent exit " + ($rc|tostring))}')"
   363	    fi
   364	    break
   365	  done
   366	  end_ms="$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-13)"
   367	  if [[ -n "$ws" && -d "$ws" ]]; then

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the

   134	verify_corpus() {

   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()

   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)

   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:

   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())

    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))
   102	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)

    88	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
    89	    if not sorted_xs:
    90	        return None

    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))

   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)

   106	class Arm:
   107	    def __init__(self, arm_id):
   108	        self.id = arm_id

   123	    def add(self, row):

   156	        for lbl in d.get("detected") or []:

   159	    def defect_fixtures(self):
   160	        return sorted(f for f, p in self.planted.items() if p > 0 and self.cells.get(f))

   162	    def fixture_means(self):

   176	def suite_report(root, suites_dir, suite, partial, out_lines):
   177	    sdir = os.path.join(root, suite)
   178	    status = {}
   179	    sp = os.path.join(sdir, "STATUS.json")
   180	    if os.path.isfile(sp):
   181	        status = json.load(open(sp, encoding="utf-8"))
   182	    spec = load_yaml_subset(os.path.join(suites_dir, f"{suite}.yaml"))
   183	    ab = spec.get("ab") or {}
   184	    th = ab.get("threshold") or {}

   186	    trials_required = int(th.get("trials_required", 3))
   187	    max_drop = float(th.get("mean_recall_max_drop", 0.10))

   216	    out_lines.append(f"## {suite}")
   217	    out_lines.append("")
   218	    out_lines.append(f"- STATUS: `{state}`; batches: {', '.join(b.get('batch', '?') for b in status.get('batches', [])) or 'none'}")
   219	    srcs = sorted({m.get('source_commit') for m in manifests})
   220	    models = sorted({m.get('model_id') for m in manifests})

   224	                     f"min_trial_recall_max_drop {min_trial_drop}, refuted_share_max_rise {refuted_rise}, "
   225	                     f"bootstrap {bs.get('method', 'percentile')} {level} over {bs.get('resample', 'fixtures')} x{iterations}")
   226	    out_lines.append("")

   228	    base = arms.get("baseline")

   230	    base_tm = base.trial_means() if base else {}
   231	    base_spread = (max(base_tm.values()) - min(base_tm.values())) if base_tm else None

   235	    def coverage_gaps(arm):
   236	        gaps = []
   237	        for fx in sorted(planned_fx):

   246	    header = ("| arm | trials done | errors | mean recall | min | max | spread | drop vs baseline | "

   248	    out_lines.append(header)
   249	    out_lines.append("|" + "---|" * 12)
   250	    details = []
   251	    verdicts = {}
   252	    for a in order:
   253	        arm = arms[a]
   254	        fm = arm.fixture_means()
   255	        tm = arm.trial_means()
   256	        m = mean(list(fm.values()))

   275	            if base is None:
   276	                reasons.append("no baseline arm")
   277	            gaps = coverage_gaps(arm) + ([f"baseline {g}" for g in coverage_gaps(base)] if base else [])
   278	            if gaps:
   279	                reasons.append("coverage: " + ", ".join(gaps[:8]) + (" …" if len(gaps) > 8 else ""))
   280	            mods = {x for x in arm.models | (base.models if base else set()) if x}
   281	            if len(mods) > 1:

   315	            f"| `{a}` | {arm.done} | {arm.errors} | {fmt(m)} | {fmt(mn)} | {fmt(mx)} | {fmt(spread)} | "
   316	            f"{fmt(drop)} | {('[' + fmt(lo) + ', ' + fmt(hi) + ']') if lo is not None else 'n/a'} | "

   332	    out_lines.append("")

   346	def main():
   347	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   348	    ap.add_argument("--results-root", required=True)
   349	    ap.add_argument("--suites-dir", required=True)

   354	    args = ap.parse_args()

   356	    suites = [s for s in args.suites.split(",") if s] or sorted(
   357	        s for s in ("review-recall", "audit-recall") if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(args.results_root, s)))

# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue
    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
        return True
    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

detected, missed = [], []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    sites = d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]
    hit = any(path_matches(p, d["file"]) and not (b < s - 3 or a > s + 3)
              for p, a, b in cites for s in sites)
    (detected if hit else missed).append(d["id"])

planted = len(man.get("defects", []))
recall = round(len(detected) / planted, 4) if planted else None

# refuted share (1.2.0): distinct cited findings that touch no defect site and
# no fix region. Regions are (file, lo, hi) on head/ line numbers, widened ±3.
regions = []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]):
        regions.append((d["file"], s - 3, s + 3))
for fr in man.get("fix_regions", []) or []:
    try:
        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        continue
findings = sorted(set(cites))
refuted = [c for c in findings
           if not any(path_matches(c[0], f) and not (c[2] < lo or c[1] > hi) for f, lo, hi in regions)]
refuted_share = round(len(refuted) / len(findings), 4) if findings else None

# trailer → severity counts (false positives on clean fixtures)
sev = None
tm = TRAILER.search(text)
if tm:
    try:
        sev = json.loads(tm.group(1)).get("counts")
    except Exception:
        sev = None
if isinstance(sev, dict):
    fp = int(sev.get("critical", 0) or 0) + int(sev.get("high", 0) or 0)
else:
    fp = len({(p, a, b) for p, a, b in cites})
false_positives = fp if planted == 0 else 0

model = effort = None
tokens = None
try:
    ex = json.load(open(executor_path))
    model, effort = ex.get("model_id"), ex.get("effort")
    u = ex.get("usage") or {}
    # every token the call consumed: uncached input, cache writes, cache

# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue
    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
        return True
    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

detected, missed = [], []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    sites = d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]
    hit = any(path_matches(p, d["file"]) and not (b < s - 3 or a > s + 3)
              for p, a, b in cites for s in sites)
    (detected if hit else missed).append(d["id"])

planted = len(man.get("defects", []))
recall = round(len(detected) / planted, 4) if planted else None

# refuted share (1.2.0): distinct cited findings that touch no defect site and
# no fix region. Regions are (file, lo, hi) on head/ line numbers, widened ±3.
regions = []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]):
        regions.append((d["file"], s - 3, s + 3))
for fr in man.get("fix_regions", []) or []:
    try:
        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        continue
findings = sorted(set(cites))
refuted = [c for c in findings
           if not any(path_matches(c[0], f) and not (c[2] < lo or c[1] > hi) for f, lo, hi in regions)]
refuted_share = round(len(refuted) / len(findings), 4) if findings else None

# trailer → severity counts (false positives on clean fixtures)
sev = None
tm = TRAILER.search(text)
if tm:
    try:
        sev = json.loads(tm.group(1)).get("counts")
    except Exception:
        sev = None
if isinstance(sev, dict):
    fp = int(sev.get("critical", 0) or 0) + int(sev.get("high", 0) or 0)
else:
    fp = len({(p, a, b) for p, a, b in cites})
false_positives = fp if planted == 0 else 0

model = effort = None
tokens = None
try:
    ex = json.load(open(executor_path))
    model, effort = ex.get("model_id"), ex.get("effort")
    u = ex.get("usage") or {}
    # every token the call consumed: uncached input, cache writes, cache

@@ -4,8 +4,9 @@
 #
 # tools/check-prompt-budget.sh enforces the byte budgets of the always-loaded
 # prompt surface: SKILL.md ≤ 16,384 B (charged with unconditionally-read
-# resources), CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 10,240 B, protocols total ≤ 200,000 B (warn
-# above 143,360 B). Passes at exactly the limit, fails one byte over.
+# resources), CLAUDE.loa.md ≤ 10,240 B, protocols total ≤ 160,000 B (warn
+# above 114,688 B). Passes at exactly the limit, fails one byte over.
+# PB-10 pins the workflow's header comment to the tool's constants.
 # PB-9 is the live gate: red until the Sprint 3 audit lands.
 # =============================================================================
 
@@ -108,3 +109,16 @@ fill() {  # fill <path> <bytes> — exactly <bytes> bytes of text
     echo "$output"
     [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
 }
+
+@test "PB-10 the workflow header comment states the tool's four budget constants" {
+    local wf="$PROJECT_ROOT/.github/workflows/check-prompt-budget.yml" line nums header n f
+    line="$(grep -E '^SKILL_LIMIT, LOA_LIMIT, PROTO_FAIL, PROTO_WARN = ' "$TOOL")"
+    [ -n "$line" ] || { echo "constants line not found in $TOOL"; return 1; }
+    nums="$(sed 's/.*= //' <<< "$line" | tr ',' ' ')"
+    [ "$(wc -w <<< "$nums" | tr -d ' ')" -eq 4 ]
+    header="$(awk '/^on:/ { exit } /^#/ { print }' "$wf")"
+    for n in $nums; do
+        f="$(LC_ALL=C awk -v n="$n" 'BEGIN { s = ""; while (length(n) > 3) { s = "," substr(n, length(n) - 2) s; n = substr(n, 1, length(n) - 3) } print n s }')"
+        [[ "$header" == *"$f B"* ]] || { echo "workflow header comment does not state $f B (tool constant $n)"; return 1; }
+    done
+}

diff --git a/base/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md b/head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md
index 077ac1b..67a159c 100644
--- a/base/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md
+++ b/head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md
@@ -1,3 +1,14 @@
+---
+paths:
+  - "**/*.sh"
+  - "**/*.bats"
+  - ".claude/scripts/**"
+  - ".claude/hooks/**"
+origin: enacted
+version: 1
+enacted_by: cycle-083
+---
+
 # Git Stash Safety
 
 `git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

+  - ".claude/agents/**"
+  - ".claude/data/agent-types.yaml"
+  - ".claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh"
+origin: enacted
+version: 1
+enacted_by: cycle-083
+---
+
 # Skill Frontmatter Invariants
 
 SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Path-scoped rule files (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-3.1, DEC-0129): stash-safety.md and
# skill-invariants.md carry `paths:` frontmatter, the frontmatter parses, and every glob
# matches at least one tracked file of the kind the rule is about (git pathspec glob
# semantics: `**` spans directories, `*` stays inside one).

setup() {
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
    RULES="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
}

# The YAML between the first two '---' lines (empty when the file has none).
frontmatter() { awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit } /^---$/ { if (n++) exit; next } n' "$1"; }
globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }
tracked() { git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" ls-files -- ":(glob)$1"; }

@test "RP-1 both rule files open with frontmatter that parses and lists string globs under paths:" {
    local f n
    for f in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
        [ "$(head -1 "$RULES/$f")" = "---" ] || { echo "$f has no frontmatter"; return 1; }
        frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.' - >/dev/null || { echo "$f frontmatter does not parse"; return 1; }
        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | type' -)" = "!!seq" ]
        n="$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | length' -)"
        [ "$n" -ge 1 ]
        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '[.paths[] | select(type != "!!str")] | length' -)" -eq 0 ]
    done
}

@test "RP-2 the globs are the ones the SDD names" {
    [ "$(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '**/*.sh **/*.bats .claude/scripts/** .claude/hooks/** ' ]
    [ "$(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md .claude/agents/** .claude/data/agent-types.yaml .claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh ' ]
}

@test "RP-3 every stash-safety glob matches a tracked shell source" {
    local g hits
    while IFS= read -r g; do
        hits="$(tracked "$g" | grep -E '\.(sh|bats)$' | head -1)"
        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked .sh/.bats file"; return 1; }
    done < <(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md")
}

@test "RP-4 every skill-invariants glob matches a tracked skill, agent definition or capability file" {
    local g hits
    while IFS= read -r g; do
        hits="$(tracked "$g" | grep -E '(^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$|^\.claude/agents/[^/]+\.md$|^\.claude/data/agent-types\.yaml$|^\.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities\.sh$)' | head -1)"
        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked file of the intended kind"; return 1; }
    done < <(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")
}

@test "RP-5 path-scoping removed no rule text: the body after the frontmatter keeps its heading and sections" {
    local body
    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/stash-safety.md")"
    [[ "$body" == *"# Git Stash Safety"* && "$body" == *"## Judgment rules the fence cannot express"* ]]
    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")"
    [[ "$body" == *"# Skill Frontmatter Invariants"* && "$body" == *"## The invariant"* ]]
}

@test "RP-6 the rule-lifecycle validator accepts both files (origin, version, enacted_by)" {
    run "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-rule-lifecycle.sh" --json
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
   151	      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
   152	               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
   153	               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
   154	else
   155	  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
   156	  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
   157	    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
   158	fi

head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:263 — The `rule_files` toggle cannot fail. head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:243 — The `companion_voice` toggle sets both `code_review` and `security_audit` to false but only checks `code_review`. The audit-side half of the toggle is never verified.
head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:72 — Every model in `models_used` with non-zero output now counts as "executor model id skew". The CLI's helper calls (haiku) produce output, and `execute-agent.sh:411-416` was written so that "a haiku helper call must not be mis-attributed". The new rule turns any A/B whose CLI made a helper call into an invalid comparison (exit 2). `execute-agent.sh:349` pins only `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, not the small/fast helper model, so this will happen in practice.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:144 — The same auxiliary-model skew rule here makes every control arm `inconclusive` ("model skew") as soon as one trial in the arm or the baseline used a helper model. The pre-registered verdicts can then never be reached.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:301 — The verdict rule is not the pre-registered one. `review-recall.yaml:60-62` says "a violated condition reads `recall loss`". The report instead turns a violated recall rule into `inconclusive` whenever |mean drop| <= the baseline's trial-to-trial spread. That is a new escape hatch added after registration, and it can hide a real recall loss, e.g. when the CI upper bound or the min-trial rule fails with a small mean shift.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251 — Re-running an existing batch with the same source and model is allowed. It re-plans every trial and appends to `<arm>/results.jsonl` (line 408), while the DONE/FAILED counters and STATUS.json restart from zero. `arms-report.py` reads every row, so duplicate trials fill the `trials_required` coverage, skew the per-trial means, and a batch with earlier failures can read `complete`. Refuse the re-run, or deduplicate/resume by (fixture, arm, trial).
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314 — The transport-failure check greps `agent-output.json`, which holds the model's own final result text, for words like `network`, `lock`-free `5[0-9][0-9] ` and `overloaded`. A review that mentions "network" or a "500 " line, on a non-zero CLI exit, is classified as a transport failure and retried, which hides agent errors. Limit the match to stderr and structured error fields.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:287 — `aggregate_status` gives up silently after 50 lock attempts and returns 0. The suite-level STATUS.json, which `report.sh --arms` and the Sprint 2 gate trust, can be left stale (e.g. `running` or `complete` from an earlier batch) with no error.
head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:502 — `outside_repo` compares the audit row's `cwd` (the hook logs the logical `$PWD`) against `ROOT`/`MAIN_ROOT`, which are canonicalised with `pwd -P` (lines 113, 461). In a checkout reached through a symlink (e.g. macOS /var → /private/var, symlinked home or workspace dirs), every block counts as "cwd outside the repository", so every real catch becomes a likely FP and `real_blocks_30d` reads 0.
head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2 — The new `paths:` scope (`**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, scripts/hooks) means the rule only loads when shell files are touched. The stash hazard does not depend on file type. The incident this rule cites (#555) was four Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to a stash wrap, and NOTES.md matches none of the globs. After this change the rule is absent in exactly the scenario it was written for.
head/.claude/skills/planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md:58 — The kind token goes after the `⇐ <blockers>` marker, and line 52 says that marker line "becomes the --deps flag when the task is created as a bead". head/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:28 — The implementing-tasks app-zone permission changes from `read` to `read-write`. content.text:
I wrote the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 13 findings, verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. All of it comes from reading the code. I couldn't run the bats suites, because the frozen PR doesn't include the files they need (`settings.json`, `lib/md-fence.awk` and the rest of the repository).

**Why it can't merge:** the control-arm experiment, which is the main point of the sprint, can give wrong or unusable results.
- **An arm can quietly run as the baseline.** The `rule_files` toggle in `execute-agent.sh` passes even when there is nothing to remove, although the PR promises that a toggle that can't take effect stops the trial. The Karpathy and companion-voice toggles are also not fully checked after they run.
- **The verdict rule is not the pre-registered one.** `arms-report.py` turns a violated recall rule into "inconclusive" when the drop is within the baseline's own spread. The suite file says any violated condition reads "recall loss".
- **Helper-model calls now count as model skew.** In both `compare-ab.py` and `arms-report.py`, any helper model that produced output counts as skew. Only the subagent model is pinned, so ordinary helper calls would make A/B comparisons invalid and arm verdicts inconclusive.
- **`run-arms.sh` miscounts in three ways.**
  - Re-running a batch appends duplicate result rows while the status counters start again from zero.
  - A failure is treated as a network/transport problem if the model's own output mentions words like "network".
  - The suite status file can silently go stale.

**Smaller findings:**
- **Symlinked checkouts:** `guard-yield.sh` compares a canonical repo path with the logical `$PWD` the hook logs. In a checkout reached through a symlink, every real block counts as a likely false positive.
- **Stash rule scoped too narrowly:** `stash-safety.md` now only loads when shell files are touched. The incident it cites was lost NOTES.md edits, which none of its globs match.
- **Template token placement:** the sprint template puts `kind:` after the `⇐` blockers marker, and that marker line is documented as the source of bead dependencies. I couldn't see the dependency parser, so this is a risk to check rather than a confirmed break.
- **Unexplained permission change:** the implementing-tasks skill's app-zone permission goes from `read` to `read-write`. The PR description doesn't mention it.

The guard register is internally consistent: the fence markers, validator markers, origin map and floor list all match, and the `floor.yaml` checksum matches its pin.
